 Judgment

This appeal by the claimants in M.V.C. No.2515/2011 on the file of I Additional District Judge and Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-II, Belagavi (for short, 'the Tribunal'), is directed against the impugned judgment and award dated 22.06.2015 whereby the aforesaid claim petition filed by the claimants was dismissed on the ground of lack/want of territorial jurisdiction on the part of the Tribunal to entertain and adjudicate upon the claim petition.

2. The material on record discloses that the appellants are the wife and children of late Ilias Shaikh,
who died in a road traffic accident that occurred on 09.10.2010 when the Maruti Alto car bearing registration No.GA-05/B-0141 driven by late Ilias Shaikh was hit by a MSRTC bus bearing registration No.MH-20/B-9060 on account of rash and negligent driving of the aforesaid bus resulting in the demise of late Ilias Shaikh.

The said claim petition was opposed by the respondents on various grounds including stating that the Tribunal did not have NC: 2023:KHC-D:10571-DB territorial jurisdiction to entertain and adjudicate upon the claim petition.
3. After the trial, the Tribunal came to the conclusion that the accident in question was on account of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the bus owned by the respondents.
The Tribunal also came to the conclusion that the claimants were entitled to compensation in a sum of Rs.22,75,000/-.

However, the Tribunal declined to accept the contention of the appellants that they were residing at Belgaum within the territorial jurisdiction of MACT, Belgaum and consequently, proceeded to dismissed the claim petition on the ground of lack/want of territorial jurisdiction of the Tribunal.
Aggrieved by the impugned judgment and award, the claimants are before this Court by way of the present appeal.

4. A perusal of the material on record including the impugned order will indicate that the Tribunal has failed to consider and appreciate the unimpeached, uncontroverted and unchallenged evidence of claimant No.1-Safina (P.W.1), NC: 2023:KHC-D:10571-DB wife of the deceased Ilias Shaikh as well as the evidence of P.W.3-Umarsab Patvegar, the landlord of the house where the claimants were residing and other material on record which cumulatively establish that the claimants, though originally from Goa, were residing at Belgaum at the time of the accident and at the time of filing the claim petition.
Further, the respondent No.1 had not adduced any rebuttal evidence to establish that the appellants were not residing at Belagavi within the jurisdiction of the Tribunal.

Under these circumstances, we are of the view that the Tribunal committed an error in coming to the incorrect conclusion that it did not have the territorial jurisdiction to entertain and adjudicate upon the petition, and consequently, the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal deserves to be set aside and the claim petition deserves to be allowed.

3 5.

Insofar as the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is concerned, the Tribunal having found that no document was produced to prove the annual NC: 2023:KHC-D:10571-DB income of the deceased at Rs.8,00,000/-, as claimed by the claimants, considering that the deceased was carrying on agricultural activities, horticultural activities and poultry business, has rightly taken the income of the deceased at Rs.2,00,000/- per annum.

The Tribunal considering the number of dependants, who were four in numbers, and the age of deceased, who was aged 54 years as on the date of the accident, deducted 1/4th of the income towards personal expenses of the deceased,
applied the appropriate multiplier '11' and awarded a total compensation of Rs.16,50,000/-.
In our opinion, we do not find any ground to reckon the income at an higher rate and as such, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the head 'loss of dependency' is not interfered with.

6. As can be seen from the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has awarded higher compensation on the conventional heads i.e., towards 'loss of consortium', 'loss of love and affection', 'loss of estate', 'loss of expectation of life of the deceased' and towards 'funeral NC:
2023:KHC-D:10571-DB expenses.
In view of the decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited.

Vs. Pranay Sethi1 and in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Nau Ram & Ors.2, in an accidental death case, under the conventional heads,
the claimants are entitled to compensation towards 'loss of consortium (spousal & consortium)',
'loss of estate' and 'funeral expenses'.

8. In the result, we pass the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is hereby allowed in part.
ii) The impugned judgment and award, dated 22.06.2015, passed in M.V.C.
No.2515/2011 by the Tribunal dismissing the claim petition is hereby set aside.
iii) The claimants are entitled to a total compensation of Rs.18,40,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization.
iv) The respondent-Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation shall deposit the aforesaid compensation along with interest within a period NC: 2023:KHC-D:10571-DB of six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
v) On deposit of the amount by the Corporation, the appellant/claimant No.1 shall be entitled to 40% of the amount; claimants Nos.2 to 4 shall be entitled to remaining 60% of the amount in equal proportion.

25% of amount falling to the share of claimants No.1, 2 and 3 shall invested in Fixed Deposit in their in a Nationalised Bank for a period of three years and remaining 75% be released in their favour.
The entire amount falling to the share of claimant No.4 shall be invested in Fixed Deposit in her name in a Nationalised Bank till she attains the age of majority.
Registry to draw the award accordingly.
